Business decisions,
made measurable.

I'm Vennela Sirusala, a business analytics professional with a Netherlands MSc and hands-on operations experience. I turn business data — sales, customers, operations, supply chain — into decisions. My tools: SQL, Power BI, Tableau and Python.

01The journey 02Data projects 03Research 04Floor experience
Motto

"The right thing, in the right place, at the right time — without waste."

Vision

Businesses that run on evidence — decisions built on clean data, clear dashboards and honest numbers, in every sector.

Mission

To turn business data into better decisions: sharper forecasts, clearer customer segmentation, faster reporting — combining hands-on operations experience with analytics.

The journey

Baramati → Velp → Tilburg → Utrecht

Supply chains and farms run on the same question: how do you get the right thing, to the right place, at the right time, without waste? I learned it first with crops and monsoons. Now I answer it with data — for any product, in any sector.

Waypoint 01 · Baramati, India

Agriculture, from the ground up

A B.Sc. Agriculture (Hons) at the College of Agriculture and Allied Sciences, Baramati — agronomy, horticulture, plant pathology, agricultural economics. Four years of understanding production systems where the inputs are living things and the deadlines are set by the weather.

Waypoint 02 · Velp, the Netherlands · 2022

Crossing over

In August 2022 I landed in the Netherlands — via Bahrain and Frankfurt — for an exchange year in agribusiness at Van Hall Larenstein. It reframed agriculture as a chain: producers, processors, traders, retailers, and all the decisions in between.

Waypoint 03 · Tilburg · 2025

MSc in Supply Chain & Operations

An MSc in Business Administration at TIAS School for Business and Society, specialising in Supply Chain & Operations Management. My thesis brought both worlds together: what stops smallholder farmers from adopting AI? My parents flew in from India for graduation day.

Waypoint 04 · Utrecht · Today

Operations, in practice

Three-plus years on warehouse and operations floors alongside my studies — RAWEP, ALSO Group, freelance shifts across the Randstad. It's one thing to model a process; it's another to have picked, packed, counted and improved one. I bring both.

"A harvest and an order book fail the same way — too late, too much, or too little. I've worked on both." — why agriculture makes better analysts

Where it began

Baramati, India

At the Agricultural Development Trust campus with my professors — four years of agronomy, soil science and stubbornness, and the mentors who pointed me outward.

Monsoon fields

June 2022

My last fieldwork season before leaving India: a spade over my shoulder, freshly turned earth, and a monsoon sky setting the schedule — my first lesson in supply and demand.

The send-off

30 August 2022

My parents at the airport the night I left for the Netherlands. One suitcase, one admission letter, and a promise to make it count.

Flying the flag

Van Hall Larenstein, Velp

Graduation day at VHL, holding the tricolour in the library where I'd spent my exchange year. Some flags you carry; some carry you.

Never stop asking

TIAS · December 2025

The school's motto on the wall behind me — and honestly, the best three-word summary of how a farm girl from Baramati ends up an operations analyst in Utrecht.

Floriade Expo

Almere · 2022

A VHL study trip to the world horticulture expo — an entire city built to ask one question: how do we grow food without using up the world?

Mount Etna

Sicily · TIAS field study

Studying sustainability on the slopes of an active volcano — where the soil literally renews itself, and so, a little, did I.

Showing my parents Europe: three small figures under seven centuries of stone. They flew across the world for my graduation; the cathedral was a bonus.
